review_type: single AI curator; full final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: or if the deficit is explained by nonspecific performance effects, the necessity claim is disproved.
errors.issue: Explaining this reported deficit through a performance confound removes its support for necessity; it does not prove the projection is unnecessary for learning. A properly controlled, effective acquisition manipulation with precise preserved learning would be needed for that stronger result.

errors.quote: Conduct a preregistered replication with projection-specific inhibition
errors.issue: The plan names useful controls but should explicitly separate inhibition during acquisition from an uninhibited retention test and retrieval-only control. Otherwise a same-performance replication retains the learning-versus-expression ambiguity.

rationale: Accurate source scope, uncertainty and possible error chain. It avoids inferring intent and proposes both original-record recovery and a controlled biological test. One disproof rule confuses removal of evidential support with biological refutation, and temporal separation of learning and expression needs specification.
reference_guardrails: C1 authenticates the record only within the synthetic dossier. No live real-world article or author claim is inferred.
N1 and E2 establish inability to reconcile/verify, not proof that animals were duplicated, effects false or intent deceptive.
A new positive or negative replication does not identify what happened to original records. Distinguish original provenance repair from new biological evidence.
Benign explanations have no established relative probabilities in this packet and do not imply the biological result will replicate.
Reduced learned performance need not indicate failed acquisition; phase-specific manipulation and uninhibited retention/performance controls help distinguish mechanisms.
Residual learning cannot refute necessity without sufficiently effective inhibition and reliable measurement. A null requires adequate precision and valid intervention.
Necessity is conditional on task, phase and context; it does not require ruling out every conceivable compensatory route or mandating all corroborative methods.
Correctly modeled repeated measures are legitimate. The concern is unverified or incorrectly treated dependence, not that every file must originate from a different animal.
An original-record audit should reconcile contemporaneous primary evidence and rerun analysis. Recovery does not itself erase a retraction.
The reference includes optical controls as examples, but E1 does not specify the inhibition technology. Do not require invented opsin-specific methods.
